_comment_file: The session area: the tab strip, the connect progress panel, the host key dialog, the status line, the find bar, the sessions and tunnels panel, and the add-forward dialog. Fetched when the first session opens, not at startup. READ THIS BEFORE TRANSLATING THE hostKey SECTION. Those strings are the whole of what a user has to decide on when a server presents a key that contradicts the one already trusted — which is either a rebuilt server or somebody reading the session. A translation that softens 'Someone may be intercepting this connection' into 'the key is different' changes what the user believes they are agreeing to. Translate the meaning and keep the weight. The same applies to forward.exposedHelp, which is the only warning before a port on this machine is opened to the local network.

tab._comment_: One tab per session. Every label here is also a tooltip, so short wins.
tab._comment_label: Names the strip itself for a screen reader. Not visible.
tab.label: Offene Sitzungen
tab._comment_close: {name} is the connection's name, from the vault: user data, in any script.
tab._comment_accessibleName: The tab's accessible name. The colour of the status dot is never the only signal that a session is connected or has failed, so the state is said in words here as well. {state} is one of tab.state below.

state._comment_: Lower case: these are read inside tab.accessibleName and shown as the status dot's tooltip, so they are fragments rather than sentences. The capitalised standalone versions are under status.state.
state._comment_verifying: The handshake is suspended on the host key dialog, waiting for the user. Not 'checking the key' — nothing is happening until they answer.
state.verifying: wartet auf eine Entscheidung zum Hostschlüssel
state._comment_closed: The session finished without a failure. 'ended', not 'closed', because the server may have ended it rather than the user.

connect._comment_: The panel drawn while a connect is in flight. It exists because a connect through two bastions can stall at any one of them, and 'which hop?' is the only useful question.
connect.title: Verbindung zu {name} wird aufgebaut
connect._comment_route: Under the title. {target} is host:port and {hops} is the jump-host chain, both machine values. 'via' here means 'by way of these hosts'.
connect._comment_waiting: In the elapsed-time column of the stage that is suspended on the host key dialog. There is no timer running: the stage is waiting on the user.
connect._comment_running: In the elapsed-time column of a stage that has started and not finished, when no interval has been measured for it yet.
connect._comment_recordingNotice: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Shown before the session opens, which is where a recording notice belongs. It must keep BOTH halves: that recording is configured, and that this build writes nothing. A user who reads only the first half believes there is a recording to go back to; a user who reads only the second believes recording is off.
connect.recordingNotice: Für diese Verbindung ist die Aufzeichnung auf „immer“ gesetzt. Dieser Build hat keinen Rekorder, es wird also noch nichts geschrieben.
connect._comment_observedNote: Explains why the panel shows four stages and not the nine in the pipeline: every row is an event the core actually reported, and none of them moves on a timer.
connect.observedNote: Die Zeiten werden zwischen den Übergängen gemessen, die der Kern meldet; Phasen, die er zusammenfasst, werden zusammen angezeigt.

stage._comment_: The four rows of the connect panel. Each 'label' is what the stage is doing; each 'pipeline' is the caption under it. The 'pipeline' values are the stage names from docs/architecture/session-pipeline.md. They also appear untranslated in the audit log and in failure messages from the core, so a reader who searches for one should find it. Leave them as they are unless your language would make them unreadable.

acquire._comment_label: 'borrowing its credential' is literal: the credential is lent to the session for the length of the connect and given back. Not 'reading' or 'loading' it.
acquire.label: Verbindung wird aufgelöst und ihre Zugangsdaten ausgeliehen

handshake._comment_label: Verifying that the host is the host it claims to be, by its key. Not verifying the user.
handshake.label: Hostschlüssel wird geprüft

authenticate._comment_label: Here it is the user being authenticated. 'channel' is the SSH term for the stream the terminal runs over.
authenticate.label: Authentifizierung und Öffnen eines Channels

hostKey._comment_: SECURITY-CRITICAL, ALL OF IT. See the file comment. Two dialogs that must not read alike: 'unknown' is a first-use question with an ordinary answer, 'changed' is a possible interception with no ordinary answer at all.

unknown._comment_title: {host} is host:port. A question, and answerable: nothing is wrong yet.
unknown.title: Dem Hostschlüssel von {host} vertrauen?
unknown._comment_lead: Says why there is nothing to compare against, and what checking actually means. 'out of band' is the point: comparing the fingerprint against what the same connection just showed proves nothing.
unknown.lead: Remoter hat diesen Rechner noch nie gesehen, es gibt also nichts, womit sich sein Schlüssel vergleichen ließe. Prüfen Sie den Fingerabdruck gegen das, was der Server lokal ausgibt, oder gegen das, was Ihnen seine Administration genannt hat.
unknown._comment_reject: The refusal on both dialogs. 'Do not connect', not 'Cancel': cancelling suggests the attempt is merely being abandoned, and this is a decision that gets written to the audit log.

changed._comment_title: A statement of fact, not a question. There is no wording of this that may be phrased as something the user can wave away.
changed.title: Der Hostschlüssel von {host} hat sich geändert
changed._comment_lead: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Both possibilities, in this order, and the refusal to proceed. Do not soften 'intercepting' into 'unexpected' or 'may not match', and do not drop the second sentence: a user whose server really was rebuilt needs to know that is the other explanation, or they will assume the alarm is a bug.
changed.lead: Möglicherweise fängt jemand diese Verbindung ab. Die andere Möglichkeit ist, dass der Server neu aufgesetzt wurde und Ihnen niemand Bescheid gesagt hat. Remoter verbindet nicht, bis Sie entschieden haben, was von beidem zutrifft.
changed._comment_replace: The only way through this dialog, and it is deliberately heavy. 'Replace' names what happens to the trusted key.

hostKey._comment_trustedKey: Heading over the fingerprint already in the vault. 'Key' is the noun — a host key — not the verb.
hostKey._comment_offeredKey: Heading over the fingerprint the server is presenting now. 'offered' as in presented for inspection.
hostKey._comment_trustedMeta: Under the trusted fingerprint. {date} is when it was first accepted, formatted for the locale; {algorithm} is a wire name such as ssh-ed25519 and is never translated.
hostKey._comment_trustedMetaUndated: The same line when the stored timestamp will not parse. Says so rather than inventing a date.
hostKey._comment_compare: On both dialogs. The randomart is the picture form of the fingerprint; comparing it is easier than comparing 43 characters. The second sentence is the instruction that matters.
hostKey.compare: Vergleichen Sie das Randomart mit dem, was der Server lokal ausgibt. Wenn Sie es nicht über einen anderen Kanal prüfen können, fahren Sie nicht fort.
hostKey._comment_confirmLabel: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The friction is the point: the user must copy characters off the screen, which is what makes them look at the fingerprint. {count} is how many characters the core is asking for — it sends the length and never the text, so this dialog cannot fill the answer in.
hostKey.confirmLabel: Geben Sie zum Fortfahren {count, plural, one {das letzte Zeichen} other {die letzten # Zeichen}} des jetzt angebotenen Schlüssels ein
hostKey.confirmHint: Tippen Sie sie vom Bildschirm oben ab. Remoter füllt das nicht für Sie aus.
hostKey._comment_audited: In the footer of both dialogs, before the buttons. Applies to the refusal as much as to the acceptance.
hostKey.audited: Wie auch immer Sie sich entscheiden: Es wird ins Audit-Log geschrieben.
hostKey._comment_algorithm: Field label. The value beside it is a wire name such as ssh-ed25519.
hostKey._comment_fingerprint: Field label. SHA-256 is the hash function's name and stays as it is.
hostKey._comment_randomart: Field label. Randomart is OpenSSH's name for the ASCII picture drawn from a key. Keep the name if your readers would recognise it; it is what ssh-keygen calls it.
hostKey._comment_deciding: On the button while the decision is being sent to the core.
hostKey._comment_decisionRefused: Title over the core's own message when it would not take the decision. The core's sentence follows underneath.

status._comment_: The one-line status bar for the session in front. Everything in it is measured or reported, never estimated.

state._comment_: Standalone and capitalised, at the head of the bar. The lower-case fragments used inside a tab's accessible name are under tab.state.

status._comment_echo: Echo latency. 'echo' is the unit of meaning here, not a unit of measurement: it says WHICH latency this is. Keep it short — it sits in a status bar next to five other figures.
status._comment_echoUnknown: The same slot before a keystroke has been sent, so there is nothing to have measured. The dash is not a zero.
status._comment_echoTitle: Tooltip on both. The second sentence is why the interface does not claim a network round trip: nothing the core reports carries one.
status.echoTitle: Zeit vom zuletzt gesendeten Tastendruck bis zum nächsten Ausgabebild. Keine Netzwerk-Umlaufzeit: Der Kern meldet keinen Latenzwert.
status._comment_transfer: Bytes in and out of this tab, counted by the interface. Used twice: in the status bar and in the Transferred column of the sessions panel, which is why it is one string and not two. The arrows are the direction and are not mirrored for a right-to-left layout — they mean received and sent, not left and right. {in} and {out} arrive already formatted with their units.
status._comment_uptimeTitle: Tooltip on the elapsed-time figure. Lower case: it labels a value rather than starting a sentence.
status._comment_authTitle: Tooltip on the username. {method} is how authentication succeeded — publickey, agent, password, keyboard-interactive — as the protocol names it, never translated and never what was sent.
status.hostKeyTitle: Der Handshake wurde gegen einen Schlüssel abgeschlossen, dem dieser Tresor vertraut.

recordingPolicy._comment_: The connection's resolved recording policy, shown in a status bar. Lower case, and fragments rather than sentences.
recordingPolicy._comment_on_request: Recorded only when the user asks for it, per session.

status._comment_recordingTitle: Tooltip on the recording badge. The second half must survive translation: this build surfaces the policy and honours none of it.
status.recordingTitle: Die aufgelöste Aufzeichnungsrichtlinie der Verbindung. Dieser Build hat keinen Rekorder, es wird also nichts geschrieben.
status._comment_rendererTitle: Tooltip on the renderer note. WebKitGTK is the browser engine the window runs on and is a product name.
status.rendererTitle: Welchen Renderer das Terminal bekommen hat. WebKitGTK kann einen software-gerasterten WebGL-Kontext herausgeben, dies ist also die geprüfte Antwort und nicht die angenommene.

renderer._comment_: What the terminal is drawing with, shown in the status bar and in the session panel. WebGL and DOM are the two technologies and are never translated; the reasons are prose and should be.
renderer._comment_notStarted: No terminal has been created for this tab yet, so nothing has been chosen. Not an error.
renderer._comment_webglNamed: {adapter} is the graphics adapter's own name, such as 'Apple M2'. Never translated.
renderer._comment_domWithReason: {reason} is one of renderer.reason below. The reason is always shown when there is one: 'it fell back' without 'why' is not actionable.

reason._comment_: Why the terminal is not on the GPU. Lower case: each one is a fragment after a separator.
reason._comment_software: The context exists but is drawn by the CPU, which is slower than the DOM renderer for a terminal. This is the case the whole check exists for.
reason.software: der WebGL-Kontext wird per Software gerastert
reason._comment_addonRefused: The context was fine but the terminal's WebGL addon would not start on it.

surface._comment_: The session area itself, and the notices that sit above it in the chrome rather than over it.
surface._comment_terminalLabel: The accessible name of one tab's terminal. Not visible.
surface._comment_failedTitle: Over the core's own failure message, which follows underneath and is not translated here.

endedReason._comment_: Why a session finished, when it finished without a failure. Each says who ended it, because that is the question being answered.
endedReason.disconnected: Der Server hat die Verbindung geschlossen.
endedReason.application_exit: Remoter hat diese Sitzung beim Beenden geschlossen.
endedReason.failed: Die Sitzung endete mit einem Fehler.
endedReason._comment_panicked: SECURITY-RELEVANT. A session whose task panicked is destroyed whole and never resumed, precisely so half of a corrupted state cannot be carried forward. Both guarantees in the second sentence are promises the core keeps and the user is entitled to rely on: keep them explicit. 'zeroized' means the secrets were overwritten in memory, not merely dropped.
endedReason.panicked: Der Task der Sitzung ist in eine Panic gelaufen und wurde zerstört statt fortgesetzt. Seine Sockets sind geschlossen und seine Geheimnisse im Speicher mit Nullen überschrieben.
endedReason._comment_aborted: It was given time to shut down cleanly, did not, and was killed.
endedReason.aborted: Die Sitzung hat ihre Frist zum sauberen Beenden überschritten und wurde abgebrochen.

surface._comment_reconnect: Verb. Opens the same connection again in this tab.
surface._comment_closeTab: Verb. Dismisses the tab; the session is already over by the time this is on screen.

certificate._comment_: SECURITY-CRITICAL, ALL OF IT. An RDP server presented a certificate that is neither pinned to this connection nor signed by an authority this machine trusts — which is what almost every Windows host presents, so this is the dialog between a working RDP session and no RDP session at all. It is the certificate half of the hostKey section above and must carry the same weight: it is a FIRST USE, answered by comparing a fingerprint against something the server did not also supply. There is no 'replace' here. A certificate that contradicts one already pinned is raised as a changed HOST KEY instead, and goes through hostKey.changed with its typed confirmation — do not borrow wording that would make this dialog look like a way past that one.
certificate._comment_title: {host} is the address being connected to, host:port. A question, and answerable: nothing is wrong yet, this machine has simply never been seen before.
certificate.title: Dem Zertifikat von {host} vertrauen?
certificate._comment_lead: Shown when the certificate can be accepted. Says why there is nothing to compare against and what checking actually means. 'out of band' is the whole point: comparing the fingerprint against what the same connection just showed proves nothing at all. 'pinned' is the word for what accepting does — the certificate is remembered for this connection, and a different one later raises an alarm.
certificate.lead: Remoter hat sich mit diesem Rechner noch nie verbunden, es gibt also nichts, womit sich sein Zertifikat vergleichen ließe. Beim Annehmen wird dieses Zertifikat fest an diese Verbindung gebunden: Wird später ein anderes vorgelegt, hält Remoter an und sagt es Ihnen.
certificate._comment_leadRefused: Shown instead when the reason is one that a first-use accept cannot answer — revoked, malformed, or a certificate that contradicts a pinned one. There is no button behind this sentence, and there must not be.
certificate.leadRefused: Dieses Zertifikat kann hier nicht angenommen werden. Ein Fingerabdruckvergleich beantwortet die Frage „Ist das der Rechner, den ich meinte?“, und das ist nicht die Frage, die dieses Zertifikat aufwirft.
certificate._comment_reasonLabel: Field label over the reason the certificate did not validate.

reason._comment_: The closed set the core reports, from remoter_proto::CertificateProblem. Each is a statement of fact about the certificate, not a judgement about the user.
reason._comment_selfSigned: The ordinary case on an internal Windows host: the certificate vouches for itself. Not a fault, and the reason pinning exists.
reason.selfSigned: Es ist von sich selbst signiert – das legt ein Windows-Rechner vor, solange ihm niemand ein eigenes Zertifikat gegeben hat.
reason._comment_untrustedRoot: Signed by an authority this machine does not trust — commonly an organisation's own internal authority.
reason.untrustedRoot: Es wurde von einer Stelle signiert, der dieser Rechner nicht vertraut.
reason.expired: Es liegt außerhalb des Zeitraums, in dem es gültig ist.
reason._comment_nameMismatch: The certificate is for some other name than the one being connected to. Say both halves: it is valid, and it is not for this.
reason.nameMismatch: Es ist gültig, aber nicht für diese Adresse.
reason._comment_revoked: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The issuer has withdrawn this certificate, which is a statement that the key behind it should no longer be used. Do not soften it, and do not imply it can be waved through.
reason.revoked: Seine ausstellende Stelle hat es widerrufen. Das heißt, dass der Schlüssel dahinter von niemandem mehr verwendet werden sollte.
reason.malformed: Es konnte nicht gelesen werden, es gibt darin also nichts zu prüfen.
reason._comment_changed: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Should never reach this dialog — a contradicted certificate is raised as a changed host key — but if it ever does, it gets no accept, and this sentence is why.
reason.changed: Es widerspricht dem Zertifikat, das bereits an diese Verbindung gebunden ist – das ist entweder ein Abfangen der Verbindung oder ein neu aufgesetzter Server.
reason._comment_unnamed: A reason this build has no sentence for. {reason} is the core's own word for it, printed as itself so a bug report can name it. A reason nobody wrote copy for never gets an accept button.

certificate._comment_fingerprint: Field label over the fingerprint. SHA-256 is the hash function's name and stays as it is.
certificate._comment_compare: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The instruction that makes the accept a decision rather than a click. Keep the second sentence: without it the first reads as advice.
certificate.compare: Vergleichen Sie diesen Fingerabdruck mit dem, was Ihnen die Administration des Rechners genannt hat, oder mit dem, was der Host selbst lokal ausgibt. Wenn Sie ihn nicht über einen anderen Kanal prüfen können, fahren Sie nicht fort.
certificate._comment_noAccept: Shown in place of the comparison instruction when there is no accept. Says plainly that the only way on is to fix the certificate, not to insist.
certificate.noAccept: Remoter verbindet sich nicht mit diesem Zertifikat. Reparieren oder ersetzen Sie das Zertifikat auf dem entfernten Rechner und verbinden Sie sich dann erneut.
certificate._comment_accept: The confirming button. Names what happens — the certificate is pinned — rather than saying 'OK'.
certificate._comment_reject: The refusal. 'Do not connect', not 'Cancel': cancelling suggests the attempt is merely being abandoned, and this is a decision that gets written to the audit log. Same wording as hostKey.unknown.reject, deliberately.
certificate._comment_decisionRefused: Title over the core's own message when it would not take the decision. The core's sentence follows underneath.

prompt._comment_: A question the connection stops at and that is answered by typing: a password when none is stored, the passphrase of an encrypted private key, or a keyboard-interactive round (RFC 4256) — a one-time code, an expired password. What is typed goes to this attempt only and is never saved. A certificate question is NOT one of these; it gets the dialog above.
prompt._comment_passwordTitle: {host} is the address being connected to, shown as written.
prompt.passwordLead: Für diese Verbindung ist kein Passwort gespeichert, deshalb fragt der Server danach.
prompt._comment_passphraseLead: The passphrase that unlocks a private key file — not the account's password.
prompt.passphraseLead: Der Schlüssel, mit dem sich diese Verbindung anmeldet, ist verschlüsselt. Seine Passphrase entsperrt ihn für diesen Versuch.
prompt._comment_challengeLead: Keyboard-interactive: the server's own question follows, verbatim. Often a one-time code or an expired-password change.
prompt.challengeLead: Die Frage des Servers steht unten — oft ein Einmalcode oder ein neues Passwort.
prompt._comment_serverText: Introduces the server's own words, shown verbatim underneath. Ends in a colon for that reason.
prompt.sendFailed: Die Antwort hat die Sitzung nicht erreicht
prompt._comment_notSaved: The footer line of the dialog. Must stay true: nothing typed here is stored anywhere.
prompt.notSaved: Nur für diesen Versuch. Nichts, was Sie hier eingeben, wird gespeichert.
prompt._comment_cancel: Verb. Gives up the connect attempt that is waiting on this question.

surface._comment_reconnectNotice: Written into the terminal's own scrollback at the point the old session stopped, between two horizontal rules that this string does not include. The scrollback is kept across a reconnect, so without this mark the new session's first output reads as a continuation of the old one. Lower case, one or two words: it is a marker, not a sentence.
surface._comment_inputRefused: Over the core's message when a keystroke was not delivered — a frozen session, most often. Says what did not happen rather than 'an error occurred'.
surface.inputRefused: Der letzte Tastendruck hat den Server nicht erreicht
surface._comment_clipboardFailed: A heading over the core's own message when a copy or paste in the terminal could not reach the system clipboard.
surface.clipboardFailed: Die Zwischenablage konnte nicht verwendet werden

framebuffer._comment_: The screen an RDP or VNC session is seen on, and driven from. Keys and clicks go to the remote host while this screen has focus, so the strings under input describe a live rule the user has to be able to act on, not decoration. RDP and VNC are protocol names and are never translated.
framebuffer._comment_label: The accessible name of the remote screen. Not visible. {name} is the connection's name, from the vault: user data, in any script.
framebuffer.label: Entfernter Bildschirm für {name}
framebuffer._comment_toolbarLabel: Names the tab's toolbar for a screen reader — the row of controls between the tab strip and the remote screen, where the send-key and scale buttons live. Not visible. The controls are there, and not over the picture, because a remote desktop uses all four of its own edges.

input._comment_: The keyboard and pointer of a live graphical session. clickToType and capturing occupy the same slot at the inline end of the tab's toolbar, above the picture, and are read one after the other by the same person: the first says how to start, the second says what changed once they did. Neither is ever drawn over the remote screen — a remote desktop uses all four of its own edges, so there is nowhere on it that is free.
input._comment_clickToType: Shown while the remote screen does not have keyboard focus, and only until the first time it is clicked. It is an instruction, not a warning: clicking the screen is what sends keys to it, and once that has been done it has nothing left to say.
input.clickToType: Klicken Sie auf den Bildschirm, um darin zu tippen
input._comment_capturing: Shown while it does have focus. IMPORTANT: say both halves — that the keys are the remote host's now, and how to reach Remoter's own shortcuts anyway. A user who cannot find the way back reads the application as hung. {prefix} is the terminal prefix as the user has it bound, e.g. Ctrl+Alt, and is never translated.
input.capturing: Tastendrücke gehen an den entfernten Bildschirm. Drücken Sie zuerst {prefix} für die Tastenkürzel von Remoter.
input._comment_sendKeys: Names the group of send-a-combination buttons for a screen reader.
input._comment_ctrlAltDel: On the button. These are key names as they are printed on a keyboard in your language — Strg+Alt+Entf in German, for instance. Keep it short: it sits on a small button.
input._comment_ctrlAltDelHelp: Tooltip. Say why a button exists for something the user has keys for: their own computer takes this combination before any application can see it, so pressing it would lock the local machine instead of the remote one.
input.ctrlAltDelHelp: Strg+Alt+Entf an den entfernten Computer senden. Auf Ihrer Tastatur wirkt diese Kombination auf diesen Computer, sie lässt sich deshalb nur von hier aus senden.
input._comment_altTab: On the button beside it. Key names again.
input._comment_altTabHelp: Tooltip. Same reason as above: the local window manager takes Alt+Tab first.
input.altTabHelp: Auf dem entfernten Computer das Fenster wechseln. Ihre eigene Fensterverwaltung fängt Alt+Tab ab, bevor dieses Fenster es sieht; es lässt sich deshalb nur von hier aus senden.

framebuffer._comment_viewOnly: Badge on a session whose saved settings say view-only. Lower case, two words, the shortest true label.
framebuffer.viewOnlyHelp: Diese Verbindung ist als „nur ansehen“ gespeichert, es wird darüber also nichts an den entfernten Host gesendet.
framebuffer._comment_viewOnlyNotice: SECURITY-RELEVANT. The standing notice on a view-only session, beside the badge. A statement of fact in the present tense: this session does not send, and the screen is live all the same. Do not soften it to 'input may not work' — a user who believes they are typing into a production server and is not has been misled either way.
framebuffer.viewOnlyNotice: Diese Sitzung ist als „nur ansehen“ gespeichert. Das Bild ist live, aber nichts, was Sie tippen oder klicken, wird an den entfernten Computer gesendet.
framebuffer._comment_stale: Shown when the sequence counter skipped, which means the core dropped a frame under load and part of the picture is older than the remote screen. Says what is wrong with what is on screen, and that it repairs itself.
framebuffer.stale: Ein Einzelbild ist ausgefallen, ein Teil dieses Bildes kann deshalb veraltet sein. Beim nächsten vollständigen Bildaufbau wird es repariert.
framebuffer._comment_awaitingFirstFrame: Before the first frame has arrived. The session is connected; there is simply nothing to draw yet.
framebuffer._comment_noContext: This window could not create the drawing surface at all. A real failure and worded as one, because the alternative is a black rectangle with no explanation.
framebuffer.noContext: Dieses Fenster konnte keine Zeichenfläche anlegen, der entfernte Bildschirm lässt sich deshalb nicht anzeigen. Den Tab zu schließen und neu zu öffnen kann helfen; es zu melden ist nützlicher.
framebuffer._comment_pointerShape: Label beside a small picture of the pointer the remote host has set. Shown only where that shape cannot become this window's own cursor — on a view-only session, whose remote pointer is not where the local one is, and on a shape too large for a cursor. It is worth showing: an hourglass means the far end is busy.
framebuffer.pointerShapeHelp: Die Zeigerform, die der entfernte Host gesetzt hat. Sie wird hier angezeigt, statt als Ihr Mauszeiger verwendet zu werden, weil Ihr Zeiger den dieser Sitzung nicht führt.

scale._comment_: How the remote screen is fitted into the tab. Each label is a control and each Help is its tooltip. Keep the labels short — they sit in a row of four to six.
scale._comment_label: Names the group of controls for a screen reader.
scale.label: Entfernten Bildschirm skalieren
scale._comment_smart: Verb-less label. Only offered when the server opened the channel that performs it, so it is never a button that does nothing.
scale._comment_smartHelp: Tooltip. Say that the remote desktop itself changes size, not the picture of it — that is the difference from Fit.
scale.smartHelp: Den entfernten Host bitten, seinen Desktop auf die Größe dieses Tabs zu bringen. Das Bild bleibt scharf, weil nichts skaliert wird.
scale._comment_fitHelp: Tooltip. 'never enlarged' matters: a desktop smaller than the tab is left at its own size rather than blown up.
scale.fitHelp: Den ganzen Desktop unter Wahrung seiner Seitenverhältnisse auf den Tab verkleinern. Ein Desktop, der kleiner ist als der Tab, wird nie vergrößert.
scale._comment_actual: 1:1 is a ratio and is written the same way in most languages; if yours writes ratios differently, use that form.
scale._comment_actualHelp: Tooltip. Says what you gain and what it costs.
scale.actualHelp: Ein entfernter Bildpunkt je Bildschirmpunkt; ist der Desktop größer als der Tab, wird gescrollt.
scale._comment_zoom: The name of the mode, used where the mode has to be named rather than picked. The buttons themselves are zoomStep.
scale._comment_zoomStep: On each magnification button. {factor} is 2, 3 or 4. The multiplication sign is notation, not a word.
scale._comment_zoomHelp: Tooltip on the magnification buttons. The reason for whole numbers only is worth keeping: a fractional zoom blurs text that was drawn for a pixel grid.
scale.zoomHelp: Um ein ganzzahliges Vielfaches vergrößern, damit kleine Schrift scharf bleibt. Eine gebrochene Vergrößerung würde sie verwischen.
scale._comment_fixedSize: A chip beside the scale controls, shown only when the picture leaves empty space in the tab AND nothing here can change the remote desktop's size — a VNC server, or an RDP one that refused the resize channel. It answers the question the user asks at exactly that spot: 'why does Fit not fill the tab?' Keep it short; it sits in a toolbar row beside the buttons. Do not soften it into 'the picture may not fill the tab' — the point is that this is the server's size, not a fault.
scale.fixedSize: Dieser Server legt seine Größe selbst fest
scale._comment_fixedSizeHelp: Tooltip on that chip. Say all three: nothing here can change the remote size, so the whole screen is shown with its proportions kept; a matching resolution is what fills the tab; and stretching the picture is deliberately not offered because it blurs remote text.
scale.fixedSizeHelp: In dieser Sitzung kann nichts in diesem Tab die Größe des entfernten Desktops ändern. Deshalb wird der ganze Bildschirm mit seinen Proportionen gezeigt und daneben bleibt Platz frei. Füllen kann den Tab nur ein entfernter Desktop mit denselben Proportionen; das Bild zu verzerren würde den entfernten Text verwaschen.

close._comment_: The question asked before a connected session is disconnected — from a tab's close button, a middle click, the close shortcut, the sessions panel, and the window's close control. A disconnect cannot be undone and interrupts work on the remote machine, so these strings must NAME WHAT IS AT STAKE rather than ask 'are you sure'. Do not shorten them into a generic confirmation.
close._comment_tab: One tab, one session. {name} is the connection's name from the vault and {target} is host:port as the server reported it — both are data, in any script, and neither is translated. bodyNoTarget is the same sentence for a session whose address is not known yet.

tab.title: {name} trennen?
tab.body: Damit endet die Sitzung auf {target} sofort. Was auf dem entfernten Rechner läuft, wird an Ort und Stelle unterbrochen, und ein erneutes Verbinden startet eine neue Sitzung.
tab.bodyNoTarget: Damit endet die Sitzung sofort. Was auf dem entfernten Rechner läuft, wird an Ort und Stelle unterbrochen, und ein erneutes Verbinden startet eine neue Sitzung.

close._comment_window: Closing the whole window. ONE question for every session, never one per tab: {count} is how many are still connected, and saying the number is the whole point.

window.title: {count, plural, one {Fenster schließen und # Sitzung trennen?} other {Fenster schließen und # Sitzungen trennen?}}
window.body: Das Schließen des Fensters beendet jede noch verbundene Sitzung. Jede wird an Ort und Stelle unterbrochen, und ein erneutes Verbinden startet eine neue Sitzung.
window._comment_listLabel: Names the list for a screen reader. Not visible.
window._comment_transfers: The total across every session in the window's question, under the list. Each row says its own count as well.
window.transfers: {count, plural, one {# Dateiübertragung läuft noch und wird abgebrochen.} other {# Dateiübertragungen laufen noch und werden abgebrochen.}}

close._comment_transfers: SECURITY-RELEVANT in the sense that matters here: it is the one thing the session knows it would destroy. Shown under the sentence above when a file transfer on this session is still queued or moving. Do not soften 'will be cancelled' into 'may be interrupted'.
close.transfers: {count, plural, one {In dieser Sitzung läuft noch # Dateiübertragung, die abgebrochen wird.} other {In dieser Sitzung laufen noch # Dateiübertragungen, die abgebrochen werden.}}
close._comment_rowTarget: One line of the window's list. {name} is the connection's name and {target} is host:port; the preposition is the only translated part.
close._comment_rowNoTarget: The same line for a session whose address is not known.
close._comment_confirm: The destructive button for one session. A verb, short.
close._comment_confirmWindow: The destructive button when the window is closing too.
close._comment_cancel: The safe answer, and the one focus lands on. Say what staying means rather than 'Cancel' — a dialog with Cancel and Disconnect makes the reader work out which is which.
close._comment_busy: On the destructive button while the sessions are being closed.

framebuffer._comment_: What the interface says when a frame from the core could not be read. Each of these means the byte stream is not the shape the format defines, which is a defect rather than a network condition — so each says plainly that the picture may be wrong, and none of them blames the user or the server.

decode._comment_: One sentence per failure. They are shown over the session, so they are short. Keep them distinguishable from each other: which one appears is the first thing a bug report needs.
decode.shortHeader: Ein Einzelbild kam zu kurz an, um gelesen werden zu können. Das Bild kann veraltet sein.
decode.shortDescriptors: Die Regionstabelle eines Einzelbildes war abgeschnitten. Das Bild kann veraltet sein.
decode.unknownEncoding: Ein Einzelbild verwendete eine Kompression, die dieser Build nicht kennt. Das Bild kann veraltet sein.
decode.unknownFormat: Ein Einzelbild verwendete eine Pixelanordnung, die dieser Build nicht kennt. Das Bild kann veraltet sein.
decode.payloadMismatch: Der Inhalt eines Einzelbildes passte nicht zu der Größe, die es angegeben hat. Das Bild kann veraltet sein.
decode.unknownMessage: Ein Einzelbild unbekannter Art kam an und wurde ignoriert.
decode.cursorShape: Eine Zeigerform kam in einer Form an, die dieser Build nicht lesen konnte.

warning._comment_: What a session warned about, shown in the session's own chrome above the picture — never over it, because a remote desktop uses all four of its edges. A count is always visible and opens the rest. SECURITY-CRITICAL IN PART: vncSecurityNone, vncCleartextRoutable and rdpNlaDisabled each describe a session that is not protecting something the user is likely to assume is protected. Translate the consequence, not just the fact. VNC, RFB, RDP and the algorithm names are protocol vocabulary and are never translated.
warning._comment_count: The one-line summary above the set. English says '1 notice' and '2 notices' alike; other languages do not.
warning.count: {count, plural, one {# Hinweis aus dieser Sitzung} other {# Hinweise aus dieser Sitzung}}
warning._comment_hide: Verb, on the control that folds the set away. It is only offered when none of them is severe.
warning._comment_unnamedDetail: Shown under a warning this build has no sentence for. {key} is the core's own identifier for it, printed as itself so a bug report can name it. Do not translate the key.

kind._comment_: The fallbacks, used when the core names a warning without a detail this build recognises.
kind._comment_unencryptedTransport: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Something about this session is travelling in the clear and the core did not say which part.
kind.unencryptedTransport: Ein Teil dieser Sitzung läuft unverschlüsselt. Wer zwischen diesem Rechner und dem entfernten Host sitzt, kann mitlesen.
kind._comment_weakAlgorithm: {algorithm} is the algorithm's name as it appeared on the wire, from the far end. Never translated.
kind.weakAlgorithm: Diese Sitzung hat {algorithm} ausgehandelt, was schwächer ist als die Algorithmen, die Remoter bevorzugt hätte.
kind._comment_recordingStarted: Sent before anything is written, which is where a recording notice belongs.
kind._comment_outputThrottled: Diagnostic, not a failure: nothing is lost, the far end is being made to wait.
kind.outputThrottled: Der entfernte Host sendet schneller, als dieses Fenster es annehmen kann; er wird deshalb ausgebremst. Es geht nichts verloren.
kind._comment_banner: Introduces the server's own login banner, which follows verbatim in its own block. Untrusted text: it is never part of this sentence.
kind.banner: Der Server hat beim Öffnen der Sitzung eine Meldung angezeigt:
kind._comment_other: A warning this build has no sentence for. The core's own identifier follows underneath.
kind.other: Die Sitzung hat etwas gemeldet, wofür dieser Build keine Formulierung hat.

detail._comment_: The named warnings the protocol adapters actually raise. Each maps to a constant in crates/remoter-proto-vnc or crates/remoter-proto-rdp, so the set is finite and closed.
detail._comment_vncCleartextLoopback: RFB with no encryption, to this machine. The least serious of the three: nothing leaves the machine.
detail.vncCleartextLoopback: Diese VNC-Sitzung ist unverschlüsselt, sie verlässt diesen Rechner aber nicht.
detail._comment_vncCleartextPrivateNetwork: The middle case: it leaves the machine, onto a network the user may or may not control.
detail.vncCleartextPrivateNetwork: Diese VNC-Sitzung ist unverschlüsselt und läuft über das lokale Netz. Alles in diesem Netz kann mitlesen, was auf dem Bildschirm steht und was getippt wird.
detail._comment_vncCleartextRoutable: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Unencrypted RFB to an address on the public internet. Do not soften this one.
detail.vncCleartextRoutable: Diese VNC-Sitzung ist unverschlüsselt und läuft über das öffentliche Internet. Alles auf dem Bildschirm und alles Getippte ist unterwegs mitlesbar. Leiten Sie sie stattdessen durch einen SSH-Tunnel.
detail._comment_vncSecurityNone: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The server asked for no authentication at all and the connection was made anyway.
detail.vncSecurityNone: Dieser VNC-Server hat überhaupt keine Authentifizierung verlangt, es hat also nichts nachgewiesen, wer sich da verbindet. Wer den Port erreicht, kann denselben Bildschirm öffnen.
detail._comment_vncVersionLegacy: The RFB version floor was lowered deliberately; say so rather than implying a fault.
detail.vncVersionLegacy: Dieser Server spricht eine RFB-Version, die älter ist als die, die die Spezifikation beschreibt.
detail._comment_vncPasswordTruncated: VNC's own authentication uses at most eight characters of a password, silently. The user's longer password is not being used in full.
detail.vncPasswordTruncated: Die VNC-Authentifizierung verwendet nur die ersten acht Zeichen eines Passworts. Der Rest Ihres Passworts wurde nicht verwendet.
detail.vncBell: Der entfernte Host hat seinen Signalton ausgelöst.
detail._comment_vncClipboardSubstituted: RFB carries clipboard text in Latin-1 only, so anything outside it cannot be sent as it was written.
detail.vncClipboardSubstituted: Einige Zeichen konnten nicht an die entfernte Zwischenablage gesendet werden und wurden ersetzt. VNC überträgt nur Latin-1-Text.
detail.vncClipboardMangled: Die entfernte Zwischenablage enthielt Zeichen, die VNC nicht übertragen kann; was angekommen ist, ist deshalb nicht genau das, was kopiert wurde.
detail._comment_vncButtonUnsupported: RFB has no way to carry the back and forward buttons on a mouse, so a press of one goes nowhere.
detail.vncButtonUnsupported: VNC kann die zusätzlichen Maustasten nicht übertragen; die Vor- und Zurück-Taste tun in dieser Sitzung deshalb nichts.
detail._comment_vncResizeUnsupported: The server does not speak the RFB extension that changes the desktop size, so Smart has nothing to ask it. The same fact as rdpDisplayControlUnavailable, on the other protocol.
detail.vncResizeUnsupported: Dieser VNC-Server kann die Größe seines Desktops nicht ändern; die Größe dieses Tabs ändert sie deshalb nicht. Mit „Einpassen“ oder „1:1“ sehen Sie trotzdem den ganzen Bildschirm.
detail._comment_vncInputUnsupported: The session was sent input of a kind RFB has no way to carry — a byte stream, which is the terminal's shape and not a framebuffer's. A statement about the protocol, not about the user's keyboard.
detail.vncInputUnsupported: VNC überträgt Tastendrücke und Zeigerbewegungen, sonst nichts. An diese Sitzung wurde etwas anderes gesendet, das nicht zugestellt werden konnte.
detail._comment_vncClipboardViewOnly: This connection is configured view-only, so it sends nothing at all — including a paste. Names the setting, because the fix is in the connection's own settings.
detail.vncClipboardViewOnly: Diese Verbindung steht auf „nur ansehen“, es wird also nichts an den entfernten Host gesendet – auch kein Einfügen.
detail._comment_vncClipboardRefused: The clipboard policy, not the protocol, refused this. The policy is the user's own setting; say which direction was refused is not possible here, so the sentence stays general.
detail.vncClipboardRefused: Die Zwischenablage-Richtlinie dieser Verbindung lässt diesen Vorgang mit der Zwischenablage nicht zu, es wurde deshalb nichts gesendet.
detail._comment_vncClipboardUnsupported: RFB carries clipboard text and nothing else: no files, and no way to ask the remote host for what it has copied. Both refusals arrive under this one key.
detail.vncClipboardUnsupported: VNC überträgt nur Text der Zwischenablage. Dateien lassen sich darüber nicht anbieten, und die entfernte Zwischenablage lässt sich nicht auf Anfrage lesen.
detail._comment_rdpNlaDisabled: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Without Network Level Authentication the credentials go to whatever answered the port, before anything has proved it is the right machine. Network Level Authentication is Microsoft's name for the mechanism; keep it, and keep NLA if your language uses the abbreviation.
detail.rdpNlaDisabled: An dieser RDP-Verbindung ist die Authentifizierung auf Netzwerkebene (NLA) abgeschaltet. Die Zugangsdaten gehen deshalb an das, was am Port geantwortet hat, bevor es nachgewiesen hat, was es ist.
detail._comment_rdpKeyboardLayoutGuessed: This build could not work out which keyboard layout this machine uses, and the session is running on US English. The server decodes the scancodes this client sends using the layout the connection names, so on any other keyboard the wrong characters appear and nothing reports a fault — which is why this is stated rather than left silent. Say what the user can do about it: the layout is a setting on the connection.
detail.rdpKeyboardLayoutGuessed: Remoter konnte nicht feststellen, welches Tastaturlayout dieser Rechner verwendet; diese Sitzung nimmt deshalb US-Englisch an. Auf jeder anderen Tastatur schreiben manche Tasten das falsche Zeichen. Stellen Sie das Tastaturlayout an der Verbindung ein, um das zu beheben.
detail._comment_rdpDisplayControlUnavailable: Not a security matter: the server did not open the channel that lets the desktop be resized. It explains why Smart does nothing on this server.
detail.rdpDisplayControlUnavailable: Dieser Server hat den Kanal, der die Größe seines Desktops ändert, nicht geöffnet; die Größe dieses Tabs ändert sie deshalb nicht. Mit „Einpassen“ oder „1:1“ sehen Sie trotzdem den ganzen Bildschirm.
detail._comment_sshAgentForwarding: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Agent forwarding was switched on for this connection and has taken effect. Anyone with root on the remote host can use the forwarded agent to authenticate as this user elsewhere, for as long as the session is open. Keep that consequence; 'agent forwarding is enabled' alone tells the user nothing they can act on.
detail.sshAgentForwarding: Die Agent-Weiterleitung ist für diese Sitzung eingeschaltet. Wer administrativen Zugriff auf diesen Host hat, kann Ihre Schlüssel darüber verwenden, solange die Sitzung offen bleibt.
detail._comment_sshInputUnsupported: The mirror of vncInputUnsupported: an SSH session was sent key or pointer input, which a byte-stream protocol has no way to carry.
detail.sshInputUnsupported: SSH überträgt einen Strom von Bytes. An diese Sitzung wurden Tasten- und Zeigerereignisse gesendet, die nicht zugestellt werden konnten.
detail._comment_sshClipboardRefused: Same wording as the VNC one, deliberately: it is the same policy, refusing the same thing, on a different protocol.
detail.sshClipboardRefused: Die Zwischenablage-Richtlinie dieser Verbindung lässt diesen Vorgang mit der Zwischenablage nicht zu, es wurde deshalb nichts gesendet.
detail._comment_sshClipboardUnsupported: A terminal has no clipboard channel: a paste is typed into the stream, and there is nothing to read back. Offering files has no meaning at all.
detail.sshClipboardUnsupported: Eine Terminalsitzung hat keine eigene Zwischenablage. Die entfernte Zwischenablage lässt sich nicht lesen, und Dateien lassen sich ihr nicht anbieten.

find._comment_: Find in the terminal's scrollback. Not a modal: the session keeps running behind it.
find._comment_label: Names the bar for a screen reader and labels its field. 'scrollback' is the terminal's history of past output.
find.label: Im Scrollback suchen
find._comment_placeholder: In the empty field. An instruction to the user, so it is the verb.
find._comment_noMatch: Beside the field when the text is not in the scrollback. Lower case: it is a note, not an error.

terminalMenu._comment_: The menu a right click opens over a terminal on macOS and Linux (and Shift+right-click on Windows). Items are the ones GNOME Terminal and Terminal.app offer; use the words your platform's own terminal menus use. Shortcuts beside them are drawn by the application and are not in this file.
terminalMenu.label: Terminal
terminalMenu._comment_find: Opens the find bar over the scrollback. The ellipsis means more input follows, as in native menus.
terminalMenu._comment_clearScrollback: Erases the terminal's history of past output on this computer. It does not touch anything on the server.

panels._comment_: One panel, two panes: what is running, and what ports are open on this machine.
panels._comment_label: Names the panel for a screen reader.
panels.label: Sitzungen und Tunnel
panels._comment_sessions: Pane name, with a count beside it. Plural noun.
panels._comment_tunnels: Pane name. A tunnel here is a port forward, the SSH -L/-R/-D kind.

column._comment_protocol: The column holds SSH, RDP, VNC or SFTP, none of which is translated.
column._comment_uptime: How long the session has been up.
column._comment_transferred: Bytes in and out since the tab opened.
column._comment_size: The terminal's size in columns and rows, e.g. 80×24.
column._comment_route: The jump hosts the session goes through, outermost first. A column and not a tooltip: when a session is slow, this is the first thing worth knowing.
column._comment_type: Which way a forward points: local, remote or dynamic.
column._comment_forward: The forward itself, written as 'where it listens → where it sends'.
column._comment_via: Which connection the forward runs on.
column._comment_connections: How many connections are open through this forward right now. The heading is abbreviated because the column is narrow; abbreviate as your language would.

direction._comment_: Badge on each forward. The letters are the ssh(1) flags and are what a reader will recognise, so they stay: -L, -R, -D.

panels._comment_direct: In the Route column when a session goes straight to its target with no jump host.
panels._comment_echoValue: The Echo column's cell. Unitless in the heading, so the unit is here.
panels._comment_echoNote: Tooltip on the Echo column. The short form of status.echoTitle.
panels.echoNote: Zeit vom letzten Tastendruck bis zum nächsten Ausgabebild.
panels._comment_noSessions: Empty state for the sessions pane. It says how to start one, because 'nothing here' on its own leaves the user nowhere.
panels.noSessions: Nichts ist offen. Doppelklicken Sie im Baum eine Verbindung, um eine zu starten.
panels._comment_focus: Verb: bring that session's tab to the front. Not the noun.
panels._comment_disconnect: Verb. Ends the session, which also closes its tab.
panels._comment_addForward: Verb. Opens the dialog under 'forward' below.
panels._comment_bindNote: Beside the Add forward button. 127.0.0.1 is the loopback address and stays as it is.
panels.bindNote: Neue Weiterleitungen binden an 127.0.0.1, sofern Sie das nicht ändern.
panels._comment_exposed: SECURITY-CRITICAL. On a forward whose listener can be reached from the local network rather than only from this machine. It is one of three signals on that row, and the only one a colour-blind reader gets. Do not shorten it to 'exposed'.
panels._comment_socks: In the destination column of a dynamic forward, which has no fixed destination: it decides per connection. SOCKS5 is the protocol's name.
panels._comment_serverListener: On a remote forward, whose listening socket is on the far end and so cannot be reported from here.
panels.serverListener: der Listener liegt auf dem Server
panels._comment_remoteBind: A remote forward that asked for port 0 and was given one by the server. {bind} is what was configured, {port} the port actually chosen.
panels._comment_inactive: In the connection count of a forward that is up but is carrying nothing. Not an error, and not the same as 'not running'.
panels._comment_stopped: In the traffic column of a forward that is no longer running.
panels.tunnelsFailed: Die Weiterleitungen konnten nicht gelesen werden
panels._comment_openCount: Footer of the sessions pane. English says '1 open' and '2 open' alike; other languages do not.
panels.openCount: {count, plural, =0 {nichts offen} one {# offen} other {# offen}}

forward._comment_: Opening a port forward. A forward runs on a connection of its own, so it belongs to a saved connection rather than to an open tab.
forward.title: Portweiterleitung öffnen
forward.lead: Die Weiterleitung läuft über eine eigene Verbindung und bleibt deshalb bestehen, unabhängig davon, ob eine Sitzung zu diesem Host offen ist.
forward._comment_connection: Field label. Which saved connection the forward is built on.
forward._comment_connectionHelp: 'hop by hop' means through each jump host in that connection's chain, authenticating at every one.
forward.connectionHelp: Die Weiterleitung authentifiziert sich als diese Verbindung, Sprung für Sprung.

directionOption._comment_: The three kinds of forward. The flags are ssh(1)'s and never change; the sentence after the dash says what each one does in terms of where the port is and what it reaches.
directionOption.local: Lokal (-L) – ein Port hier erreicht einen Host so, wie die Gegenstelle ihn sieht
directionOption.remote: Entfernt (-R) – ein Port auf der Gegenstelle erreicht einen Host so, wie wir ihn sehen
directionOption.dynamic: Dynamisch (-D) – ein SOCKS5-Proxy hier, der über die Gegenstelle hinausgeht

forward._comment_bindAddress: Field label. The local address the forward listens on.
forward._comment_destinationHostHelp: Which machine looks the name up. A name that resolves here may not resolve there, and that is the mistake this prevents.
forward.destinationHostHelp: Wird vom entfernten Host aufgelöst, nicht von diesem Rechner.
forward._comment_destinationHostPlaceholder: An example host name in the empty field, not a real one. Replace it with an example that reads naturally to your readers if this one does not.
forward._comment_exposed: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The label on the tick that permits a non-loopback bind. It is deliberately long: the user is accepting a consequence, not setting an option, and the consequence is named in the label rather than hidden in a tooltip.
forward.exposed: Über Loopback hinaus binden und hinnehmen, dass das lokale Netzwerk diese Weiterleitung erreichen kann
forward._comment_exposedHelp: SECURITY-CRITICAL. 0.0.0.0 means every network interface on this machine. Keep 'every device on the network' — it is what makes the risk concrete — and keep the second sentence: the core will not bind at all without this tick, so the user is not being warned after the fact.
forward.exposedHelp: Eine an 0.0.0.0 gebundene Weiterleitung öffnet jedem Gerät im Netzwerk einen Weg in diesen Rechner. Ohne dieses Häkchen verweigert der Kern das Binden.
forward.noConnections: Dieser Tresor hat keine Verbindungen, über die sich eine Weiterleitung öffnen ließe.
forward._comment_portInvalid: Under a port field. The range is the TCP one and does not change between languages.
forward.portInvalid: Ein Port ist eine Zahl von 1 bis 65535.

duration._comment_: Compact elapsed times: an uptime that ticks in a status bar, and the time one connect stage took. Two units at most, and the letters are abbreviations of the unit's name — use your language's, and keep them short enough for a narrow column. Every number arrives already written in the locale's own digits and with its own decimal separator, so place it and do not reformat it.
duration._comment_daysHours: Days and hours, e.g. '1d 6h'. Minutes are dropped at this scale because nobody is counting them.
duration._comment_milliseconds: A connect stage under a second. ms is the SI symbol for millisecond and is not translated; the space before it is.
duration._comment_elapsedSeconds: A connect stage over a second, e.g. '4.2 s'. s is the SI symbol for second.
